title: Department of War releases UFO files on Trump's order
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Department of War releases UFO files on Trump's order, about 2026 at United States (no place named), and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: On May 8th, 2026, [music] the Department of War released hundreds of UFO-related documents, video, and audio with President Trump ordering the release of government files related to ET life and UFOs,
We're at an unprecedented time in UFO history where the president is actively contemplating releasing documents, which they clearly have, on on these unidentified flying objects.
tellings.difference: Says the president is still thinking about releasing the documents, where the story says the Department of War released them on May 8, 2026.
tellings.link_reason: Both are about President Trump releasing government UFO files in 2026.

as_told.title: President contemplating release of UFO documents

tellings.quote: so the first trunch, that's what you saw is a bunch of videos from drones from MQ9 Predator drones where they've cited something that seems really strange,
tellings.difference: Says the first batch was MQ-9 Predator drone videos and credits Stephen Miller.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe the 2026 Department of War / White House release of UFO files ordered by Trump. This telling covers the first batch.

as_told.title: First White House release of MQ-9 drone UAP videos

tellings.quote: on the UFO files that Trump has done three of them now. All the photos and videos have these big blacked out rectangles.
tellings.difference: Says there have been three releases so far and that the photos and videos carry large blacked-out rectangles.
tellings.link_reason: Both are about the 2026 government UFO file releases ordered by Trump.

as_told.title: Trump-era UFO file releases with blacked-out camera data

tellings.quote: It's again, it's still it's a work in progress with the pursue files. Again, there's no metadata there, but there's a whole lot of UAP activity in those videos and reports.
tellings.difference: Gallaudet calls the release the PURSUE files, says it is still a work in progress with no metadata, and stresses that the videos and reports hold a lot of UAP activity.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of the government's recent release of UAP files and videos; PURSUE is the release Gallaudet describes as full of UAP activity. The orb report story is a single case inside it.
